solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Left one protected by upper‑class European

indicators.note: something protected is shielded on all sides, so the upper-class word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: posh is everyday British slang for upper-class
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A snobbish European aristocrat shelters someone who has been abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole, from Poland, is described with this nationality adjective, so it names a European.

clue.text: Cleopatra is excited after casting off her last breastplate!

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
casting off drops something, here the final letter of the queen's name

explanation.surface: Cleopatra gets so worked up that she throws off her armour.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEOPATRA without its final A leaves CLEOPATR, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is an ornament or armour plate worn on the chest, so it serves as a breastplate.

clue.text: Evidence of loss from brewing a keg ale

indicators.note: brewing mixes and works ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A barrel of beer that is being made loses some of its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the escape of a liquid or gas, which shows that something is being lost.

clue.text: Eastern county rowing crew rumoured to choke

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: Suffolk is a county in eastern England and an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Gossip says a rowing team from East Anglia lost its nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'choke' fits the sporting surface as losing under pressure; it means to stifle. Suffolk is an English county on the east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To choke someone is to cut off their air, the same as stifling them.

clue.text: Worker runs to trap savage fox

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside, so the worker-plus-runs letters close around the savage word

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker
savage and wild both describe untamed creatures
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A labourer sets off running to catch a wild fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fox' looks like the animal being hunted, but it is a verb meaning to puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle or confuse them, a straightforward verbal synonym.

clue.text: Bush says people must be respected politicians

parts.note: the elder is a shrub or bush
to state is to say
men are people

explanation.surface: A President Bush insists that people should honour political figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Bush' suggests the American president; it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names veteran politicians whose experience earns them general respect.

clue.text: Discovered mint with money mainly for South Americans

indicators.note: read as dis-covered, the word has its covering, its outer letters, removed
mainly means most of, so the last letter goes

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Someone found newly made coins and banknotes destined for South America.
explanation.walkthrough: MINT without its outer letters gives IN; CASH loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people of the Andean empire in Peru.

clue.text: Get separated from fantastic creature in plunge

indicators.note: the creature is put inside the word for a plunge

parts.note: a dive is a plunge
an orc is a monster from fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A diver splits off from a mythical beast during a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce someone is to legally end a marriage and be separated from them.

clue.text: Give up and put a coat on before decorating

definitions.meaning: to hand over or surrender something

definitions.text: put a coat on before decorating
definitions.meaning: builders apply a base coat of plaster to a wall before it is decorated

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to hand over and to plaster a wall with a first coat.

clue.text: For energy, limits the amount of rapid increases

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
life means energy or liveliness
to ration supplies is to limit the amount of them

explanation.surface: A policy statement about restricting power use.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is a rapid spread or multiplication, so the plural means quick increases.

clue.text: Fuelled from a source of lignite dismissed by company

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so take its opening letter

parts.note: an employee who is fired has been dismissed

explanation.surface: Talk of a firm sacking workers at a brown-coal power plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A power station run on coal is fuelled by it, so the hyphenated adjective describes how it is powered.

clue.text: Group that spell 'bay' with an 'n'?

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay
the letter given as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about spelling a word for a bay with an extra letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' pretends to be about writing letters, but in the definition it is a magic spell, cast by a group of witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of witches is the classic group that casts spells together.

clue.text: Having some luck working with a cob

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
a cob is a round loaf, a kind of bread roll in British usage

explanation.surface: A baker gets lucky while working with a round loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a run of successes, a spell of good luck.

clue.text: Wine kept for man on bench?

definitions.meaning: a wine laid down and kept to mature is labelled as such
a substitute player sits on the bench waiting to come on

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a matured wine set aside and a substitute sportsman waiting on the bench.

clue.text: Agree to drop regulars and name a venue

indicators.note: dropping the regularly spaced letters keeps only every other one, starting from the first

explanation.surface: People consent to drop the usual guests and pick a place to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the second and fourth letters of AGREE leaves ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue for sport or entertainment, a place where events are staged.

clue.text: American army dress — overweight, I reckon, not quite complete

parts.note: fat means overweight

indicators.note: something not quite complete is missing its final piece, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to reckon is to guess or estimate

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a GI's uniform is a bit too tight around the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: GUESS loses its final S to give GUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigues are the loose working uniform of soldiers, a term especially common in US army use.

clue.text: Fighter delighted a riot's broken out

parts.note: glad means delighted

indicators.note: something broken is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word riot, the 's being has

explanation.surface: A spectator is pleased that a disturbance has erupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman arena combatant, a fighter by trade.

clue.text: Doctor Brown on Italian thriller

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the long-running BBC series
dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A physician called Brown writes about an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Brown' reads as one person's name; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story, the classic kind of mystery thriller.

clue.text: Scottish engineer admitting mistake with a boatman

indicators.note: admitting lets someone in, so the engineer's name opens to take in the other letters

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer confesses to an error involving someone who rows a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratty, the boat-loving water rat in The Wind in the Willows, famously says there is nothing like messing about in boats.
explanation.definitionFit: The river-dwelling character Ratty spends his days in boats, so he is the story's boatman.

clue.text: Circus performer, born in a European setting

indicators.note: the letter for born goes into the other letters
a setting holds a stone in place, so the outer letters are its mount

parts.note: a Croat is a European from Croatia

explanation.surface: A circus act is born in some European location.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs gymnastic feats, a staple act of the circus.

clue.text: It's in a church letter

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the first-named going into the middle

parts.note: the word it, with the 's standing for is as a link

explanation.surface: A notice says something is posted inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Part of arable farming's up to date

parts.note: till means until, up to a time
an age is a period or date in history

explanation.surface: Part of farming on ploughed land is up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the ploughing and cultivation of land for crops.

clue.text: Short of verve

definitions.meaning: in Britain a short is a small measure of strong liquor such as whisky

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strong distilled drink and liveliness or vigour.

clue.text: Protective cover for primate in role

indicators.note: the primate is placed inside the word for a role

parts.note: an actor's role is their part
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: An actor seeks shelter for playing a monkey in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along a roof, bridge or rampart.

clue.text: Quietly enthusiastic about horse

parts.note: P is the musical notation for piano, quietly
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly keen on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald horse with patches of white and another colour.

clue.text: Protective cover for child in unfinished part of playground

indicators.note: the child goes inside the shortened playground piece
something unfinished lacks its last bit, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a slide is a piece of playground equipment
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child huddles under shelter on part of an unfinished playground.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIDE loses its E to give SLID. SKID LID is British slang for a motorcyclist's crash helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a crash helmet, which protects a rider's head, so it is a protective cover.

clue.text: Bird finding love in right dump!

indicators.note: the letter for love goes inside the other letters

parts.note: to bin something is to dump it
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone finds romance while rummaging in a proper rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small red-breasted songbird.

clue.text: Prepare too hard for open rule, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the words are said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: open is overt and rule is reign, together said aloud

explanation.surface: Advice on rehearsing for an unrestricted law seems to involve noise.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who trains too much, preparing beyond what the body can take, is doing exactly this.

clue.text: Bird finally caught rodent eating it

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the other letters surround the word given
finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

explanation.surface: A bird finally catches a mouse that is devouring something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' at the start looks like the subject that caught the mouse; it is only the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmouse is an older and American name for the tit family of small songbirds.

clue.text: Man of the cloth makes enquiries, not without refusal

parts.note: someone who pries makes nosy enquiries

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the refusal is taken out of the word not

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A clergyman asks questions and will not take no for an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the cloth is a clergyman, and this word names an ordained minister.
